I see the issue. In the `in_val_string` state, the bounds check happens AFTER the `*cp == '"'` check. So if `pval` is already at the boundary and the next char is `"`, it writes `*pval++ = '\0'` which could overflow. But more importantly, let me look at the `in_escape` case with `\u` handling - it does `cp++` and reads `*cp` without bounds checking, which could read past the end of the input buffer (use-after-poison READ 1).
